# Mutable lookup and detached memory images, version 4.0

Extend the C++ system under `src/`. Its live insertion/mapping implementation
and typed memory exporter are supplied. The new capture and loaded-image APIs
are incomplete. Correct the system as needed; existing code is not a semantic
oracle. No particular repair strategy or address layout is required.

## Build and public interfaces

The environment supplies CPython 3.11.14, its standard library, and an offline
GNU C++ 9.4.0 toolchain for Linux x86_64/glibc 2.31 or newer. There is no package
installation or runtime network dependency. `python3 build.py` collects the
C++ source and compiles all `src/**/*.cpp`, with C++14, `-O2`, the `src` include
path and static C++/GCC runtime linkage. It writes `tmp/scamptrie`. It compiles
one translation unit at a time. Headers and other included source files may
be added under `src`; use one program entry point. C++ object sizes do not
represent the SRAM charges below.

Only `src/` is collected. It may contain at most 128 filesystem entries
(files and directories, excluding its root) and 4 MiB of file contents.
Every file must be regular, single-linked, UTF-8 source text; no symlinks,
hardlinks, devices or FIFOs. The tree is frozen before compilation. Generated
files belong in `tmp`, outside `src`. The fixed front end, build/check scripts,
compiler archive and other public assets are restored independently of the
submission; edits to them are not collected. No source elsewhere is collected.

After building, `python3 run.py` is the public CLI: read one UTF-8 JSON value
to EOF, write one JSON value and exit 0. The fixed front end validates syntax
and bounds, converts input to the text wire interface used by `src/main.cpp`,
and execs the compiled program. Its writer is a forked pipe producer; the
native process retains normal pipe descriptors 0 and 1. The supplied entry
point handles wire I/O and response formatting, not the missing image work.
`image_io.hpp` only reads/writes fields. The internal wire is exactly the one
implemented by the fixed front end; the external contract is the JSON below.
Alternative implementations of the specified behavior are accepted.

## Requests and state

A request is exactly `{"cases":[{"ops":[operation,...]},...]}` with 1..2 cases.
Every case begins with an empty live FIB, no saved snapshots, and an empty
loaded image. Cases are independent. An address is exactly 32 lowercase hex
digits, MSB first. Prefix lengths are integers 0..128. Hops are integers
0..4194302. Booleans are not integers. Keep every distinct normalized prefix,
even when redundant or when several prefixes have the same hop.

Operations are arrays, with no additional elements:

* `["put",address,length,hop]`: clear host bits and insert/replace that exact
  normalized prefix. The latest put wins. It changes only the live FIB.
* `["query",[address,...]]`: longest matching live-FIB prefix per address,
  or null when none matches.
* `["save"]`: emit and retain a detached compact image of the complete live
  FIB at this point. Its saved index is zero-based save order.
* `["load_saved",index]`: validate that earlier saved image and, if valid,
  replace the loaded image. A correct saved image must be accepted.
* `["load",image]`: validate a supplied image. Return false on semantic
  invalidity, leaving the previous loaded image unchanged; otherwise replace
  it and return true. Loading never changes the live FIB or saved images.
* `["image_query",[address,...]]`: look up only the loaded serialized image.
  It must not depend on a live trie or on original prefix input.

Per case: at most 133120 operations, 131072 puts, 131072 query addresses
(combined across both query kinds), 8192 distinct normalized prefixes,
3 saves and 16 loads (both kinds combined). There may be at most 4096 distinct
16-bit front keys and 4096 distinct 64-bit front keys among live prefixes.
There is no erase operation. A saved index must refer to a preceding save.
The complete request is at most 32 MiB. Validate it before executing any case.

Missing/extra object keys, wrong types/counts/bounds, invalid UTF-8/JSON,
duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers or malformed hex require exactly
`{"error":"invalid"}`. Image JSON has the shape/bounds below; violating those
is a malformed request. Bit contents, ordering, reachability, coverage, BMPs
and other image invariants are semantic validation performed by `load`.

## Responses

For a valid request, return exactly `{"results":[result,...]}` in case order.
A result is exactly `{"answers":[hop_or_null,...],"snapshots":[image,...],
"loads":[boolean,...]}`. Flatten answers across all query addresses in operation
order, including both query kinds. Snapshots are in save order; loads are in
load-operation order. Puts produce no output item. No diagnostics on stdout.

## Forests and node semantics

The three owners match the supplied system. Prefixes of length 0..16 belong
to the depth-0 root. Lengths 17..64 belong to a depth-16 root keyed by the high
16 address bits. Lengths 65..128 belong to a depth-64 root keyed by the high
64 bits. Each nonempty owner group has one root, and empty groups have none.
Lookup prioritizes a matching 64-bit front, then a matching 16-bit front,
then the depth-0 root. A missing root yields null.

Within each forest, branches consume six bits. A node reached after t edges
has global depth `origin+6*t`, where origin is 0,16 or64. A branch's local
prefixes have relative lengths l=0..5 from that node; child key v is the next
six bits. Only prefixes long enough to include all six bits enter children.
A final partial chunk is zero-padded on its right; no child may run beyond
its owner's maximum length (16,64 or128). The supplied prefix primitives
illustrate fragment extraction; all boundaries must still be correct.

A subtree with one or two owned prefixes uses TYPE4 or TYPE5 respectively.
Larger subtrees use TYPE1 with 0..2 children, TYPE2 with 3..6, or TYPE3 with
7..64. Local prefixes plus child subtrees partition the owned prefixes exactly.
There are no omitted, duplicated, leaf-pushed, merged or unreachable nodes.
Every non-root has one parent. Roots may occupy any of the 11 stages; stage
0 is the tail, 10 the head. Every child stage is STRICTLY LOWER than its parent.

Each node's BMP is the hop of the longest GLOBAL FIB prefix of length <= the
node's global depth that matches its entire region, or null. This can include
an equal-depth prefix and can cross forest ownership boundaries. BMPs do not
replace storing their owned prefixes. This convention deliberately matches
the live system's marker behavior; it is not a strict-ancestor-only BMP.

For local length l and value v, NI bitmap position is `2**l+v`. Bit0 is unused;
valid positions are 1..63. The node's NI values follow increasing set-bit
position. A case's image dictionary stores distinct used 64-bit patterns in
increasing numeric order, including zero if used. Pattern sharing never
shares node-local NI values. NI arrays with positive length are disjoint and
cover the complete NI vector without holes. Empty arrays have base0. All
patterns and NI entries must be used. Inline TYPE4/5 prefixes are not NI entries.

## Image shape and physical storage

An image has exactly these keys:

```
{"root":null_or_[stage,cell],
 "front16":[[key_hex4,stage,cell],...],
 "front64":[[key_hex16,stage,cell],...],
 "cells":[integer,...], "banks":[[word_hex64,...],...],
 "bitmaps":[mask_hex16,...], "nexthops":[hop,...]}
```

All hex is lowercase and fixed-width. Front lists each have at most4096 entries.
There are exactly11 cells/banks entries; cells are integers0..131072. Each
bank has at most65536 words, with at most65536 words across all banks. The
bitmap vector has at most8193 entries; the NI vector at most8192 hops.
Locators contain stage0..10 and cell0..131071. Fronts are sorted by numeric
key, unique, complete and tagged: software hash collisions cannot discard keys.
Every prefix represented by a loaded image obeys the same ownership/hop rules
and its complete FIB has at most8192 distinct normalized prefixes.

Each 256-bit row has two 128-bit cells. TYPE1/4 have one-cell logical size;
TYPE2/3/5 have two. All two-cell slots begin at even cell offsets. A TYPE3
chooses any subset of at most THREE direct children. All others are bulk:
there are at least four, they share one lower stage, and their roots occupy
contiguous TWO-cell slots in increasing bulk-key order. A logically half-size
bulk root still occupies two cells; its upper half is zero padding. Its
ordinary descendants are independently placed subject to topology.

Every ordinary TYPE1/4 occupies exactly one cell; every other node occupies
exactly two. Charged slots cover `[0,cells[stage])` densely and without overlap.
A bank contains exactly `ceil(cells[stage]/2)` rows. If cells is odd, the final
upper half is zero. There is no extra full-row padding or unused nonempty data.
Thus each emitted mapping uses the minimum row count for its charged slots.
Any legal stage/slot/direct-child choice meeting these rules is accepted;
there is no global placement optimum or hidden address tie-break.

## Packed fields

Words are printed as 64 hex digits MSB first; bit0 is the integer LSB. A
half record starts at bit0 or128 according to its cell offset; full records
start at bit0 of an even-cell row. The following offsets are within a record.
Every reserved bit is zero. A 22-bit BMP is a forwarding value, not a live
manager index;4194303 denotes null. Other hop fields may not use that value.

| Type | Fields from low bits to high bits |
| --- | --- |
| 1 (128 bits) | type3, BMP22, bitmap_id16, NI_base22, child32 x2, reserved1 |
| 2 (256 bits) | type3, BMP22, bitmap_id16, NI_base22, child32 x6, reserved1 |
| 3 (256 bits) | type3, BMP22, bitmap_id16, NI_base22, bulk_bitmap64, bulk_base22, bulk_stage4, direct32 x3, reserved7 |
| 4 (128 bits) | type3, BMP22, inline_prefix94, reserved9 |
| 5 (256 bits) | type3, BMP22, inline_prefix94 x2, reserved43 |

A child32 contains key6, stage4, cell22 in that LSB-first order. Present
explicit/direct children are sorted by key, followed by absent records.
The ONLY absent encoding is `15<<6`: stage15, key0, cell0. Present stages are
0..10. TYPE3's bulk bitmap has bit v set for child key v. Direct and bulk keys
are disjoint. For a bulk key, cell is `bulk_base+2*popcount(bulk_bitmap bits
strictly before that key)`; bulk_base is even. All locators resolve exactly.

An inline prefix94 contains fragment64, length8, hop22, LSB first. The fragment
is the whole normalized left-aligned 64-bit fragment relative to its forest
origin, not relative to the current node. For origin0 it contains the high
address bits, with relative length0..16. For origin16 it contains address
bits16..63 at its high end, relative length1..48; for origin64 it contains
the low64 address bits, relative length1..64. Clear all fragment host bits.
It must belong to the node region and have global length >= that node depth.
TYPE5's two records may be in either order; they must denote distinct prefixes.

The front and NI vectors make an image self-contained. A loader must validate
all graph, field, stage, ownership, compactness, NI/dictionary and global BMP
invariants, including data not used by supplied queries, before committing.
A valid empty image has null root, empty fronts/dictionaries/NI, zero cells
and eleven empty banks. A failed load preserves the previous complete image.
This CPU archive is not claimed to be bit-compatible with a hardware file
loader or to reproduce hash circuitry, FPGA timing, updates-in-flight or
packet throughput. No online erase, SA search or allocation-ratio optimization
is required. The fixed graph-depth/FIB bounds admit compact images within the
published storage bounds; valid puts/saves cannot be reported infeasible.

## Execution and isolation

The working directory is /workspace in the local chroot/container. Runtime
and source files are read-only during evaluation. Scratch tmp is fresh for
each scored request and is TMPDIR; /tmp is not promised writable. The compiled
program is frozen outside scratch by the controller. Each complete JSON request
including both cases, parsing, pipe input production and output has180s wall
time. This is a bounded control-plane replay/checkpoint maintenance batch,
with an allowance for complete image validation, rather than a packet-rate
measurement; the budget is unchanged from the prior public worker. A build has its own180s wall budget, with the same per-process CPU soft/
hard180/181s,2GiB address space,64 processes/threads per UID,256 FDs,64MiB per
regular output file and zero core dumps. Both build and program stdout are
bounded at32MiB and stderr at1MiB. No network/sockets/socketpairs. The local
worker selects the first two CPUs in its inherited allowed set; this is shared
execution capacity, not an exclusive reservation or timing rank. Use at most
two build jobs; the supplied build uses one. BLAS/OpenMP thread variables are1.

The local worker drops privilege and uses chroot/seccomp. Its syscall filter
denies socket/socketpair/connect; System V shared memory, semaphore and
message-queue calls; kill/tkill/tgkill; ptrace and process_vm_readv/writev;
unshare/setns; mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot; setsid/setpgid; UID/GID/group
changes; open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at; bpf; keyctl/add_key/request_key;
perf_event_open/userfaultfd; io_uring_setup/enter/register; pidfd_getfd.
clone3 returns ENOSYS; clone flags matching mask 0x7e820000 are denied
(namespace creation and CLONE_UNTRACED). Non-x86_64
and x32 syscall ABIs are rejected. No `/proc`, host files, tests or solutions
are mounted into that execution root. Environment variables are a clean
PATH, HOME=/workspace, LANG/LC_ALL=C, TMPDIR, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1,
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and BLAS/OpenMP thread variables set to 1.

Other inherited limits observed in the local worker are: stack 8 MiB soft,
unlimited hard; locked memory 65536 bytes soft/hard; POSIX message queues
819200 bytes soft/hard; pending signals 384572 soft/hard; nice and real-time
priority limits 0 soft/hard. Data segment, RSS and real-time CPU duration
limits are unlimited; RLIMIT_OFILE aliases the 256-FD limit. These are
disclosed host limits, not additional scoring metrics. The future formal
container backend has not been validated against this inherited-limit set.

Scratch has a sampled emergency brake at 1 GiB (logical or allocated bytes,
whichever is larger per file) or 50000 entries, including the scratch root.
Crossing it is an infrastructure error with no score, not an exact quota.
There are no local cgroup aggregate CPU/memory or exact scratch quotas;
formal container validation is pending. Use modest scratch; no persistent scratch is needed by the lookup program.


The compiler archive is a fixed public asset; it is not part of the4MiB
collected source budget. Its verified extraction is below128MiB/4096 files,
within the same scratch limits. Compiler subprocesses additionally receive
LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing only at the supplied compiler libraries and TMPDIR
pointing at their fresh build directory. The fixed front end sets the compiled
program path and its pipe-writer PID internally; no tests, answers or grader
secrets are conveyed by environment variables.

`python3 public_check.py` must run as a non-root workspace user on Linux
x86_64. It freezes the source tree, builds with only public files, then runs
the seven small public JSON requests. It is a sanity command, not hidden
scoring. Its trusted `child_run(path,data:bytes)->bytes` API still launches a
Python entry with real bounded pipes; that entry may exec the native program.
Each such child has the180s deadline above, plus at most5s supervisor cleanup.

The checker is a Linux child subreaper and puts each child into a separate
session/process group. Submitted descendants re-deny kill/tkill/tgkill and
setsid/setpgid before execution. On success, overflow, deadline, abnormal exit
or SIGINT/SIGTERM, the checker kills the complete group and reaps adopted
descendants before returning or printing a pass, even if the initial child
already exited or descendants closed0/1/2. Buffered output is drained within
the original deadline; cleanup grants no extra execution time. Repeated
interruptions cannot interrupt group cleanup. Empty/nonJSON/wrong/nonzero
output fails; ordinary text/buffer/rawfd/fileno/fdopen and flushed explicit
exit0 output are supported by the pipe supervisor.

Only the **DEVELOPMENT supervisor profile** permits the trusted checker
same-UID signaling and session/group creation (the five calls above), with
all numeric, chroot and other scored syscall limits unchanged. Its child
restores those denials. Scored compilation and CLI requests keep the default
worker profile; no candidate privilege is broadened. Using that scored worker
to host this supervisor fails closed. Ordinary non-root public execution needs
Linux prctl subreaper/seccomp support and those supervisor APIs.

A local controller must use one exclusive canonical task UID lease, verify
account/process vacancy, wait for active use, and hold the lease through all
cleanup. A whole public-command capture must allow build plus seven child
deadlines, cleanup and startup: the task maintenance allowance is1800s. This
is an outside capture allowance, not a submitted-program budget. The public
command may retain scratch across its children; scored requests receive fresh
scratch and must compute solely from that request. Genuine Docker images,
aggregate cgroups/storage quotas, artifact transport and formal production
isolation are separately unvalidated (formal_pending_docker).
